title: Choose the portfolio's new visual world
question: The roll assigned the Delivery Register. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. Open each card's preview (expand) to see the full page with your real content.

options.label: Delivery Register
options.lineage: Dhaka wholesale delivery challans and handover registers
options.thesis: Every project is a signed handover: who got it, when, what was delivered, and whether it still runs.
options.viewport: A form header with name and an open-to-roles field box holding Email and CV, one plain sentence of record, then the delivery register's first rows.
options.risk: Turns into accounting cosplay if stamps and red serials spread past status and numbering.

raised.raise: One date column runs down the whole page as its spine; every entry hangs from it.
Minor projects stay folded to a single register line and open in place.
Colour is law: red only numbers rows, stamp ink only marks live or in-development status.
Size follows billing rank: the two strongest projects take full rows, the rest set small.

options.label: Statement of Work
options.lineage: company annual reports and their results tables
options.thesis: Two years of shipped work reported like a company reports a year: a plain letter, then the results.
options.viewport: A short letter to the hiring team beside an at-a-glance results table, with Email and CV under the letter.
options.risk: The most familiar of these; close to where most serious portfolios land, and can read corporate.

options.label: Departures Board
options.lineage: airport boarding passes and live gate boards
options.thesis: Projects ranked on a live board by date, each with an honest status; the candidate holds the pass.
options.viewport: A segmented pass with name, base, role and availability above a departures board listing the products and their status.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: products map to board rows with live or in-development status; weaker on feeling mature.
options.risk: The metaphor can read playful to a conservative hiring manager.

options.label: Mesophotic Dive
options.thesis: A career as a descent, depth as time.
options.viewport: A vertical dive profile with projects pinned at depths.
options.case: Fuses poorly: hiring managers do not read a career as a dive.
options.kept: One vertical axis ruling every line.

options.label: Akari Workshop
options.risk: Soft where the brief asks for proof.
options.kept: Unlit forms fold flat until opened.

options.label: CRT Arcade
options.thesis: Projects as levels on a pixel screen.
options.viewport: A score bar and tile playfield.
options.case: Fuses poorly: the opposite of mature.

options.label: Darkroom Bay
options.case: Fuses poorly: amber gloom fights legibility.
options.kept: A fixed order of stations the reader moves through.

options.label: Double-Feature Sheet
options.thesis: Two headline projects shouting on one sheet.
options.viewport: Two titles at different scales over collage.
options.case: Fuses poorly: loud where the brief asks for mature.
options.kept: A strict billing rank that sizes every item.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean, modern engineer's site: name, plain intro, screenshot-led projects, experience, contact.
canonCard.viewport: Name and a two-line plain intro with Email and CV, then the first project with a large screenshot.
canonCard.risk: Looks like many other strong engineer portfolios.
